$comment: Generated by tools/ground-truth/analyse-metrics.ts from experiment T2. Do not hand-edit: rebuild the probe decks, re-read them through PowerPoint, and re-run the analysis.

lineModel.$comment: The rules that fit every probe of their kind. Each was chosen over the alternatives listed in `refuted`, and the analysis throws rather than emit a rule two candidates fit.
lineModel.percentQuantisation: round half up to a whole percent
lineModel.advance: percent x 1.2 x size; exact points as given  [the measured rule]
lineModel.letterSpacing: points after every character, the last included
lineModel.kerning: on when kern > 0 and size >= kern  (threshold, inclusive)

kernDefault.$comment: ECMA-376 says an omitted @kern kerns at every size. Measured, a file that states no @kern anywhere is not kerned below this threshold, because 3.1 found PowerPoint substitutes its own p:txStyles and those carry one. A resolver therefore has to read @kern through the cascade; the ECMA default only applies once the cascade has genuinely yielded nothing.

percentQuantisation.model: round to a tenth of a percent

advance.model: percent x size (the percentage applied to the font size, not the line box)
percent x 1.2 x size; exact points also scaled by 1.2
a flat 1.2 x size, ignoring a:lnSpc entirely

letterSpacing.model: em-relative: spc/100000 x size, every character

kerning.model: on when kern > 0 and size > kern  (threshold, exclusive)
a boolean: on whenever the attribute is present
a boolean: on when kern is non-zero, at any size

lastLine.$comment: Measured data, not a committed rule. The best model found is stated with its exact score and every probe it misses; `descentPt` is the per-face term it needs, which no browser reports. Finishing this is sub-phase 3.6.
lastLine.model: advance <= 1.2 * size ? max(advance, 0.75 * advance + descent) : 0.75 * advance + descent

scored.model: the advance itself (what every line above the last measures)
advance <= 1.2 size ? max(advance, 0.75 advance + c) : 0.75 advance + c

advances.$comment: PowerPoint advances in points, with the trailing paragraph mark subtracted. `paragraphMarkPt` is that mark, which equals the face space advance and is an artefact of TextRange2.BoundWidth rather than of layout.

entries.font: Zzz Probe Face That Is Not Installed
Zzz Probe Face That Is Not Installed

Zzz Probe Face That Is Not Installed

browserAgreement.$comment: How far Chromium measureText is from PowerPoint on the same face, size and string, as a fraction of the PowerPoint width. The plan promises a tracked number rather than pixel-perfection; this is that number.

perFont.font: Zzz Probe Face That Is Not Installed

readings.$comment: What PowerPoint reported, so a test can re-derive the rules above instead of asserting the sentences that describe them. `advancePt` is the distance between two line tops; `heightPt` and `widthPt` are TextRange2.BoundHeight and BoundWidth, the latter still including the paragraph mark.

substitution.$comment: The probe table names one face that is not installed. PowerPoint measures it as another face, and which one is a measurement rather than a guess. Relevant to 3.7: document.fonts.check returned true for it, so presence cannot be detected that way and an advance fingerprint is needed.
substitution.absentFace: Zzz Probe Face That Is Not Installed
